source.title: Enhancing Deep Learning with Optimized Gradient Descent: Bridging Numerical Methods and Neural Network Training
source.authors: Yuhan Ma; Dan Sun; Erdi Gao; Ning-Jing Sang; Iris Li; Guanming Huang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Table 3 is incomplete or garbled: it lists five optimizers per model but only eight mAP values, so several optimizer-to-value assignments cannot be recovered.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers using test-set task metrics, bearing on V4's held-out performance claim, but does not measure the training-to-test gap or use the original studies' recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on several tasks. Only comparisons explicitly assign test results to SGD and Adam are recorded; Table 3's ambiguous entries are not assigned to optimizers.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and SGD on held-out R8 text-classification accuracy, testing V4 in a new language-task setting. Its proposed optimizer's performance alone would not establish this relation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors conclude that TM-SGD improves on original SGD across their reported tasks and that numerical difference methods offer an interpretable, extensible way to improve optimizers. They do not establish a general Adam-versus-SGD conclusion or analyze generalization gaps. Their conclusion also mentions TM-SGD-M improvements that are not documented in the supplied results.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes TM-SGD, an optimizer based on a Taylor multi-step numerical method, and compares it with existing optimizers on task metrics; it does not test the claim's memorization or generalization-gap setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports optimizer outcomes that vary by task; Adam's comparison with SGD is favorable on the reported GAN FID and unfavorable on segmentation, text classification, and facial key-point MSE.

fits_no_version.finding: Lraspp segmentation mIoU is 68.6% with Adam versus 70.1% with SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested segmentation recipe, Adam achieves lower evaluation mIoU than SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: GAN FID is 0.0553 with Adam versus 0.0925 with SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested image-generation recipe, Adam produces better sample-quality FID than SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Facial-keypoint test MSE is 0.1320 ± 0.009 with Adam versus 0.1306 ± 0.006 with SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam and SGD have close reported facial-keypoint regression errors under this recipe; the supplied uncertainty does not establish a reliable difference.

record.peer_reviewed: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
record.problems: The study does not report training error or the train-test gap. Some comparisons use different task metrics, and Table 3 optimizer-to-mAP assignments are incomplete or ambiguous. Several task-specific numbers are reported without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 includes mAP values for Fast-RCNN and RFBNet, but the flattened optimizer/value listing does not support assigning most values to individual optimizers. No ambiguous assignments were recorded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.

Image-classification results; equal or better training performance; optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; Adam-to-SGD switching; and word-level language modeling. The experiment uses shared settings rather than documenting a tuning search.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: The R8 momentum-SGD comparator is omitted: SGD-M accuracy is 90.4%, also above Adam's 90.1%. This additionally supports V4's direction under the fixed recipe, without reported uncertainty.

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used. Segmentation, keypoint regression, and image generation are treated as outside V4's explicitly stated benchmark scope. Table 3's ambiguous assignments are already declared in rows_left_out. Image-classification experiments are listed in the setup but no corresponding outcomes are supplied. Missing training-error measurements do not prevent the R8 held-out comparison from testing V4's performance component.

versions.untested_parts: Training performance, broader hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay, and word-level language models.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: Lraspp
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD or Adam and compare test mIoU.
rows.note: The text states that TM-SGD outperformed most other optimizers and gives these SGD and Adam values.
rows.check: The numerical comparison is correct, but segmentation mIoU is outside V4's stated image-classification and language benchmarks. The supplied text also does not explicitly identify this evaluation split as held out.

rows.subject: LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD or Adam and compare test accuracy.
rows.note: The paper reports test accuracy for the named optimizers.
rows.check: The extracted state is backwards: Adam's 90.1% accuracy is below SGD's 90.6%, matching V4's direction. No uncertainty or significance test is reported.

rows.subject: GAN
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD or Adam and compare FID.
rows.note: Lower FID is stated to indicate better performance; the paper says Adam and TM-SGD outperform SGD and SGD-M.
rows.check: GAN sample-quality FID does not measure the held-out classification or language performance named in V4. The values are correctly transcribed, but cannot challenge that version.

rows.subject: PreActResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD or Adam and compare test MSE.
rows.note: The table reports lower test MSE for SGD than Adam.
rows.check: Facial-keypoint regression MSE is outside V4's stated benchmark scope. Adam's slightly higher MSE and overlapping reported uncertainty do not establish a verdict on that version.

relationships.condition: LSTM text classification on R8 with shared learning-rate, schedule, and training-duration settings
relationships.reason: R2 reports Adam accuracy of 90.1% versus SGD's 90.6%; this supports the direction under this fixed recipe, without establishing statistical significance or performance after optimizer-specific tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam accuracy is 90.1% versus SGD's 90.6%, but the comparison remains unverified and significance and optimizer-specific tuning are unestablished.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
